@andrew I tried to use msgbuf here, but I was not successful in using it. Could you please tell me if its possible to use here?
It's hard to say without knowing more details of the problem. What went wrong?
I had made a minor mistake, when extracting the msgbuf. I have pushed a patchset by using msgbuf APIs.
Hi Pavithra, I have a few comments inline.

Is there really no way this can fail? I don't think we should silently accept `NULL` as the value for `tree`, for instance. Is it an error to try to delete a node that doesn't exist? That should be discussed somewhere and be behaviour defined in the documentation.
Done, changed the API to return success or failure when deletion.
The cast is unnecessary as the formal parameter is `const void *`
Acknowledged
What assurance do we have that this is true?
Acknowledged
Please declare variables at the top of blocks, kernel-C-style.
Done
Acknowledged
Hmm, I thought we already had a helper for this comparison somewhere.
I checked the `msgbuf.h` file, I saw there where msgbuf copy, msgbuf extract, msgbuf insert APIs. I think we do not have compare msgbuf API, I might be wrong too.

This is what I was referring to:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/src/dsp/pdr.c#L1737-L1744
Done
I don't think this makes sense if `prev == start` as you have in the initial conditions on 2114 and 2115?
Acknowledged
This needs to go in the `[Unreleased]` section.
Done

This can be:

```
return pldm_msgbuf_complete_consumed(buf);
```

However, see below.
Acknowledged

Taking the address here seemed odd to me. So I looked at the definition of `pldm_entity_node`, and the type of the `entity` member is already `struct pldm_entity`, which describes all the members anyway. Now, given it's a packed struct I can only assume the value endianness is PLDM wire format (if they're host (BMC CPU) endian then we have bugs), so we still have to do the conversion, but otherwise there's no need for the msgbuf extraction, right? Just use the struct members?

The msgbuf APIs should be used where we'd otherwise cast void pointers to a packed struct. But here we don't have void pointers, we have a well-typed pointer.

This needs some discussion.

@arj Yes, we can skip using the msgbuf extraction here and directly use struct. Since we already have a defined structure (like pldm_entity) and a well-typed pointer. But I need to check if the endianness will be a problem. I think PLDM is little-endian in nature and we do the host endianness conversions in a few places -`https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/3b986d3a6829eba0c546df7035e095c7abe48ae3/src/dsp/fru.c#L64` but don't see it in the Entity Association structures.
My unit test cases passed with this change.
Yes, the tests will always pass, as the endianness is always consistent on the same processor without explicit conversions.
Acknowledged

So the endianness of all of the struct members is generally not well defined in the libpldm API. My rough approach is that values passed in packed structs need to be in the wire-format endianness, as the whole point of a packed struct is that it is to be cast over a wire-format byte buffer. So to pick any other endianness for the packed structs would lead to confusion.

However, working in wire-format endianness is not ergonomic. I'll need to think about what we do here, e.g. whether we define another struct that isn't packed that requires values in host-endianness.
Perhaps the easiest thing to do for now would be to explicitly document that the values passed in `entity` must be in host-endianness.
Acknowledged
I'd prefer this be `const pldm_entity *entity`.
Done
I don't think this is reasonable. I think this should be `-ENOENT`, and the documentation should be updated.
Done
`-ENOENT` again here.
Done
Can we call this `curr` ("current") rather than `start`?
Done
Need to `ASSERT_NE(entities, nullptr)`.
Done

The assert added threw a clang-analyzer issue `Potential leak of memory pointed to by 'entities' [clang-analyzer-unix.Malloc,-warnings-as-errors]`. Moved the pointer to be std::unique_ptr with a custom deleter which guarantes the free.
Resources acquisition and release needs to be done in stack-order. You `malloc()`ed `entities` before initialising `tree`, so you must destroy `tree` before you `free()` `entities`.
Done

As it stands entity can't be `NULL` as it's passed by value. That said, I think passing by pointer might be preferable here (i.e. `const pldm_entity *entity`), but a `NULL` pointer should be dealt with by returning `-EINVAL` and not `-ENOENT`.

The `-ENOENT` suggestion was with respect to `entity` being semantically valid, but the entity itself was not present in `tree`.
yes, I have tried to capture the return values in the doxygen, please suggest if I have missed anything
Need to test `entity` here too when changing it to a pointer.
Acknowledged
Seems a little complex when we could instead free at the end, but sure.

Can you make this a complete sentence? You have a full-stop at the end of the line above. Also the cases for `-ENOENT` are not described?

Can you please read over your work and make sure it's coherent before pushing? I'm not trying to nitpick things to death, but these issues are quite easy to spot 😞

Andrew, I am extremely sorry for not proofreading the patchset. I have created the documentation to incorporate all the return values. The `-EOVERFLOW` error was returned when we had the `msgbuf` code in the patchset. Since we moved away from it as per one of your earlier review comments, I have removed it from the documentation.
e.g. we're returning `-ENOENT` here, so the cases where we return `-ENOENT` must be described in the documentation (the implementation must conform to the documentation).
Acknowledged
This should be "-ENOENT @p entity is not found in @p tree", right? The implementation of the search might return `NULL` if it's not found, but saying `NULL` here isn't useful to the reader 😞
Acknowledged
Can you remove the blank line here?
Done
